info.bio:
Culture Club fue una banda de pop británico de los años ochenta capitaneada por Boy George quien se identificaba por su estética glam y transgresora.

Fue un grupo que triunfó en los años ochenta con temas sensuales hechos para adolescentes y fáciles de seguir por sus fans. En sus inicios, Boy George creó revuelo en sus apariciones por televisión, por sus maquillajes coloridos y por la ropa femenina y las trenzas con las que se presentaba en sus apariciones, un aspecto inequívocamente travestido.

scenes.name: Segunda invasión británica y MTV
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: En 1982 el new pop deja de ser un sueño de periodistas: «Don't You Want Me», «Tainted Love» y «The Look of Love» anuncian una nueva invasión, y en 1983 la segunda camada (Duran Duran, Culture Club, Wham!, Eurythmics, Thompson Twins) conquista Estados Unidos gracias a MTV, canal ideado por Michael Nesmith que, sin vídeos americanos, dependía de los británicos, más videogénicos y cultivados en el estilo («I want my MTV»). A Flock of Seagulls, Altered Images («Happy Birthday»), Simple Minds («Promised You a Miracle», New Gold Dream), Haircut 100, Kajagoogoo; Bowie se broncea con «Let's Dance». El new pop reexporta música negra (Chic, P-Funk, Quincy Jones) a la América blanca. En el Reino Unido, 1983 se vive en cambio como un año infausto: reelección de Thatcher, «Kill Ugly Pop» en las paredes y la vuelta de la conciencia social.

scenes.name: Synth-pop y new romantics
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Todo empieza con los instrumentos electrónicos, el futurismo melódico de Eno y los ritmos robóticos de Kraftwerk: el synth-pop es quizá el acontecimiento más importante de la música melódica desde el Mersey-beat. The Buggles («Video Killed The Radio Star»), Gary Numan, Yellow Magic Orchestra, OMD, Depeche Mode, Human League; con Soft Cell llega el diluvio y el dúo de teclista y cantante se impone (Eurythmics, Yazoo, Erasure, Pet Shop Boys). Flying Lizards y New Order («Blue Monday»). Los nuevos ídolos adolescentes, los new romantics: Duran Duran, Culture Club, Thompson Twins, Tears For Fears, ABC, Heaven 17.

scenes.name: Nuevos románticos
scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
scenes.desc: Movimiento londinense que rescata del glam el maquillaje y la pose, con un uso coyuntural de la tecnología: Ultravox (con John Foxx primero), Japan, Visage de Steve Strange, Duran Duran, Spandau Ballet, ABC, la pose kraftwerkiana de Gary Numan y, después, Culture Club.

podcast.title: Boy George's Drag and R&B Voice
podcast.body: Boy George redefined "drag" with his makeup, hat, and braids, likened to a "one man RuPaul's Drag Race about three decades early." He possessed a "remarkably supple R&B style voice," which made him a near-instant sensation upon Culture Club's debut. "You might call Boy George a one man RuPaul's Drag Race about three decades early, serving realness in his makeup, hat, and braids."

podcast.body: Culture Club was initially considered an alternative band, despite their new wave sound having stripped away much of the punk DNA. "Culture Club and WAM, both of which, by the way, were considered to be alternative bands in the very beginning."

podcast.title: Featured on 80s US New Wave Compilations
podcast.body: In the 1980s, compilations edited as "New Wave" in the United States often featured a diverse range of British bands, including Culture Club, reflecting how the term was applied to non-mainstream UK music. These compilations were often a "mixed bag" of artists. "Incluso los ex Tisí y los culturclava, vean como New Wave, muchos recominatorios en Estados Unidos."

podcast.title: Jamaican Influences in Pop
podcast.body: Culture Club incorporated numerous Jamaican influences into their pop music. Despite these foreign influences, the band did not face accusations of cultural appropriation for creating music that was not purely British. "la música a Hamayaka se asentó en lo más profundo del pop, o sea, culture club tiene muchísimas influencias a Hamayaka y nadie fue a hallacharles la bronca porque estaban haciendo algo que no era británico."

podcast.title: John Moss as Drummer
podcast.body: John Moss, who was briefly considered as a drummer for The Clash (one of 207 candidates), later surfaced as the drummer for Boy George and Culture Club. This detail connects the early punk scene with the emerging new wave and pop movements of the 1980s.

podcast.title: MTV Prominence and Style
podcast.body: Culture Club, fronted by Boy George and his unique look, was a British band that gained significant airtime on MTV, becoming a key part of the "second British invasion" that characterized the channel's early programming. "Culture Club with Boyd George's unique look..."

podcast.title: Mainstream Pop Evolution
podcast.body: After New Wave's rise on MTV, bands like Culture Club emerged, characterized by their danceable sound. This represented New Wave veering towards mainstream commercialism, significantly removed from its punk roots. "80s New Wave veered toward danceable bands like Culture Club, who were quite a distance removed from the music's punk roots."

podcast.body: Culture Club was among the artists whose videos received a "Canadian video premiere" during the launch of MuchMusic on August 31, 1984. This marked their official debut on Canada's first 24-hour music channel. "Plus, the Canadian video premiere of Yes, Elvis Costello, The Fix, Human League, Slay, Culture Club, and a few surprises."

podcast.body: The band emerged from the New Romanticism scene, which originated in London nightclubs that frequently played Technopop music. "Durand Durand came from this stew, so did the Culture Club."

podcast.title: Pioneers of New Romanticism
podcast.body: Culture Club was identified as a New Romantic group that rose from the British club circuit, specifically Billies and The Blitz Club, which were instrumental in the development of synth-based new music and associated subcultures. "One such offshoot was known as New Romantic, which had its roots in a couple of British clubs dedicated to new music. One was called Billies, and the other was the Blitz Club. This was the breeding site of groups like Spandovalet, Visage, and Culture Club."

podcast.title: Prominence in New Pop
podcast.body: Culture Club, fronted by Boy George, was a prime example of a New Pop band. Their unique visual presentation, amplified by music videos, helped them become cultural phenomena in the early 1980s. "Think Boy George and Culture Club, ABC in their Sharp Tuxedos, Orange Juice, a band of Scotland featuring Edwin Collins, Asda Camer was another, Heaven 17 was still another."

"Alan was in a Tectopop band from Chicago that had spent some time touring with both Depeche Mode and Culture Club."

xref.title: Inspiration for LGBTQ+ Individuals
xref.body: Bowie's public comments about his sexuality in 1972 struck a chord with thousands who were afraid to come out, giving them courage and a sense of shared identity with a famous figure. Figures like Boy George of Culture Club and Holly Johnson of Frankie Goes to Hollywood have stated that Bowie's comments changed their lives. "Bowie gave them the courage to be who they were."
